anharmonic-ratio.definition: Projective invariant of four collinear points or four concurrent rays introduced in this terminology by Michel Chasles and treated in Casey Book VI, Sec. VI (pp. 127–140). Equal to -1 in the case of harmonic section.

antiparallel.translation: Transversal cutting two sides at transposed base angles
antiparallel.definition: A straight line cutting AB, AC at D, E so that angle ADE = angle ACB and angle AED = angle ABC (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. I, Def., p. 169). Parallel to the tangent to the circumcircle at A and bisected by the symmedian from A.

brocard-angle.translation: cot ω = cot A + cot B + cot C = (a² + b² + c²) / (4Δ)
brocard-angle.definition: Common acute angle ω = ∠ΩAB = ∠ΩBC = ∠ΩCA = ∠Ω'BA = ∠Ω'CB = ∠Ω'AC of a triangle ABC (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. II, pp. 176–177), bounded above by 30° with equality iff ABC is equilateral.

brocard-circle.definition: The circle having the segment joining the circumcentre O = X(3) and symmedian point K = X(6) as diameter (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. V, pp. 194–195). Passes through O, K, both Brocard points Ω and Ω', and the three vertices A', B', C' of Brocard's First Triangle.

brocard-points.translation: Isogonal bicentric pair with barycentrics (1/b² : 1/c² : 1/a²) and (1/c² : 1/a² : 1/b²)
brocard-points.definition: Unique interior points Ω (first) and Ω' (second) at which the sides of ABC subtend equal oriented angles ω = ∠ΩAB = ∠ΩBC = ∠ΩCA and ω = ∠Ω'BA = ∠Ω'CB = ∠Ω'AC (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. II, pp. 175–178).

caseys-theorem.definition: John Casey's 1866 theorem (Book VI, Sec. IV, Prop. 10, pp. 103–104): four circles 1, 2, 3, 4 are tangent to a fifth circle (or straight line) iff their pairwise common tangents satisfy 12·34 ± 14·23 ± 13·24 = 0. Reduces to Ptolemy's Theorem (Euclid VI.D) when all four radii vanish.

centre-of-mean-position.translation: Weighted barycentre Σ mᵢ Pᵢ / Σ mᵢ
centre-of-mean-position.definition: Unique point G associated to weighted points Pᵢ with weights mᵢ such that for every line L, Σ mᵢ·dist(Pᵢ, L) = (Σ mᵢ)·dist(G, L) (Casey Book I, Props. 17–18, pp. 12–13).

centre-of-similitude.translation: External and internal homothetic centres dividing OO' in ratio r₁ : ±r₂
centre-of-similitude.definition: Points on the line of centres of two circles through which all direct (external) or transverse (internal) parallel-radius joins and common tangents pass (Casey Book VI, Sec. II, pp. 82–87).

coaxal-circles.translation: One-parameter pencil of circles sharing a common radical axis
coaxal-circles.definition: Family of circles every pair of which has the same radical axis (Casey Book III, Prop. 24, p. 44; Book VI, Sec. V, pp. 113–119). Classified into intersecting (common chord), non-intersecting (real Poncelet limiting points L₁, L₂), and tangent pencils.

complete-quadrilateral.translation: Four general lines meeting in six vertices with three diagonals
complete-quadrilateral.definition: Projective figure formed by four coplanar straight lines in general position, possessing six vertices in three opposite pairs and three diagonals each divided harmonically by the other two (Casey Book VI, Sec. III, Prop. 7, p. 91).

cosine-circle.translation: Six-point circle centered at K cut by antiparallels through K
cosine-circle.definition: Circle passing through the six intersections of the antiparallels through the symmedian point K with the sides of ABC (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. III, Prop. 1 Cor. 4, p. 183). Centered at K with side intercepts proportional to cos A : cos B : cos C.

euler-line.translation: Collinear axis containing O = X(3), G = X(2), N = X(5), H = X(4), and L = X(20)
euler-line.definition: Straight line on which lie the circumcentre O, centroid G, nine-points centre N, orthocentre H, and de Longchamps point L, with HG = 2·GO and HN = NO (Casey Book I, Misc. Ex. 43, p. 20; Book IV, Prop. 5).

feuerbach-point.translation: Internal contact point of the Nine-Points Circle and Incircle
feuerbach-point.definition: Point Fe = X(11) at which the Nine-Points Circle touches the Incircle internally (Casey Book VI, Sec. IV, Prop. 10 Cor. 2, pp. 104–106). On the canonical Heronian (15, 13, 14) triangle, Fe = (6, 8).

harmonic-polygon.translation: Cyclic n-gon which is the projection/inversion of a regular n-gon
harmonic-polygon.definition: Cyclic polygon inscribed in a circle possessing a generalized symmedian/Lemoine point whose distances to the sides are proportional to the side lengths (Casey 1886; Supp. Ch., Sec. VI, pp. 205–218).

harmonic-section.translation: Internal and external division in the same ratio: (A, B; C, D) = -1
harmonic-section.definition: Division of segment AB internally at C and externally at D so that AC : CB = AD : DB, equivalently AB is the harmonic mean of AC and AD (Casey Book VI, Sec. III, Def., p. 87).

harts-circle.translation: Circular-triangle generalization of the Nine-Points Circle
harts-circle.definition: Andrew Searle Hart's 1861 theorem (Casey Book VI, Sec. IV, Prop. 11, pp. 106–108): for any circular triangle formed by three circles, the eight circles touching all three partition into sets of four that are each touched by a fourth circle (Hart's Circle).

inversion.translation: Conformal involutory map P -> P' on ray OP with OP·OP' = k²
inversion.definition: Transformation with respect to a circle of inversion (O, k) sending each point P != O to P' on ray OP with OP·OP' = k² (Casey Book III, Def. p. 41; Book VI, Sec. IV, pp. 95–112). Preserves angles and cross-ratios while interchanging lines through O and lines/circles.

isogonal-conjugates.translation: Cevian pair symmetric across the internal angle bisectors
isogonal-conjugates.definition: Two points P, P' whose rays from A, B, C are reflections of one another across the angle bisectors of ABC (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. I, Prop. 1, p. 165). Their six pedal projections onto the sides lie on a single pedal circle centered at the midpoint of PP'.

isotomic-conjugates.translation: Cevian pair cutting each side at points equidistant from the side midpoint
isotomic-conjugates.definition: Points whose cevians meet BC, CA, AB in points symmetric with respect to the side midpoints Ma, Mb, Mc (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. I, Def., p. 167).

lemoine-circle.translation: Six-point circle cut on ABC by parallels to the sides through K
lemoine-circle.definition: Circle passing through the six intersections of the three parallels through the symmedian point K to the sides of ABC (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. III, Prop. 1, pp. 179–181). Centered at the midpoint of OK = X(182), with side intercepts proportional to a³ : b³ : c³.

limiting-points.translation: Zero-radius circles L₁, L₂ of a non-intersecting coaxal pencil
limiting-points.definition: Two points L₁, L₂ on the line of centres on opposite sides of the radical axis at distance equal to the tangent from the radical foot D to any circle of the system (Casey Book III, Prop. 23 Def., p. 43). Every circle of the conjugate orthogonal pencil passes through L₁ and L₂, and L₁, L₂ are inverse points with respect to every circle of the coaxal pencil.

nine-points-circle.translation: Circle (N, R/2) through midpoints, altitude feet, and Euler midpoints
nine-points-circle.definition: Circle centered at N = X(5) = midpoint(O, H) of radius R/2 passing through the three side midpoints, the three altitude feet, and the three midpoints of segments joining H to the vertices (Casey Book IV, Prop. 5, pp. 57–58).

orthogonal-circles.translation: Circles intersecting at right angles: |O₁O₂|² = r₁² + r₂²
orthogonal-circles.definition: Two circles whose tangents (and hence radii) at each point of intersection are perpendicular, characterized algebraically by d² = r₁² + r₂² (Casey Book III, Prop. 22, p. 42). Any circle orthogonal to (O, k) is mapped onto itself by inversion in (O, k).

pole-and-polar.translation: Projective point-line duality induced by a circle: (x₀-h)(x-h)+(y₀-k)(y-k)=r²
pole-and-polar.definition: For a point P != O and circle (O, r), the polar of P is the perpendicular to OP at the inverse point P' of P (Casey Book III, Def., p. 44). Governed by La Hire's Reciprocity (Prop. 25): Q lies on polar(P) iff P lies on polar(Q).

power-of-a-point.definition: Jakob Steiner's invariant PA·PB = PO² - r² for any secant PAB through P meeting circle (O, r) at A, B (Euclid III.35–36; Casey Book III, Props. 20–24, pp. 41–44).

radical-axis.translation: Linear locus of equal circle powers pow(P, C₁) = pow(P, C₂)
radical-axis.definition: Straight line perpendicular to the line of centres along which tangents (or powers) with respect to two non-concentric circles are equal (Casey Book III, Prop. 23, p. 43). For three circles with non-collinear centres, the three pairwise radical axes concur at the Radical Centre.

reciprocation.translation: Duality mapping points to polars and lines to poles
reciprocation.definition: Method of deriving dual projective theorems by replacing every point by its polar and every line by its pole with respect to an auxiliary base circle (Casey Book VI, Sec. VII, pp. 141–147), transforming Pascal's inscribed hexagon into Brianchon's circumscribed hexagon.

steiner-and-tarry-points.translation: Antipodal circumcircle pair associated with Brocard's First Triangle
steiner-and-tarry-points.definition: Parallels through A, B, C to the corresponding sides of Brocard's First Triangle concur at Steiner's Point X(99) on the circumcircle; perpendiculars concur at its diametral antipode, Tarry's Point X(98) (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. VII).

symmedian.translation: Isogonal reflection of a median; concurrency K = (a² : b² : c²)
symmedian.definition: Isogonal conjugate of a median across the internal angle bisector. The three symmedians concur at Lemoine's Point K = X(6), whose perpendicular distances to the sides are proportional to the side lengths and minimize x² + y² + z² (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. I, Props. 5–7, pp. 170–172).

tucker-and-taylor-circles.translation: One-parameter family of six-point antiparallel/parallel triangle circles
tucker-and-taylor-circles.definition: Family of circles cut on the sides of ABC by triangles homothetic to ABC with homothetic centre K, centered along OK (Casey Supp. Ch., Sec. III, pp. 181–186). Includes the Circumcircle, First Lemoine Circle, Cosine Circle, and Taylor's Circle (six projections of altitude feet onto the adjacent sides).
